title: Topic models reveal differing clinical-note trajectories around vasculitis treatment
summary: An unsupervised analysis of 113,048 notes from 660 vasculitis patients found differing documentation trajectories around treatment initiation. Kidney-inflammation mentions peaked near treatment start, whereas other manifestations were more persistent; psychiatric symptoms also appeared before treatment. These are patterns in documentation, not measured disease incidence or causal treatment effects.
ai_technology: Latent Dirichlet allocation with cross-run topic stabilization
organization: Brigham and Women's Hospital; Massachusetts General Hospital; Harvard Medical School

evidence.tested: Three learned 100-topic models yielded 90 stable topics, which two vasculitis experts independently labeled and reconciled. Notes were aligned from two years before to five years after treatment in three-month windows. Topics for glomerulonephritis peaked near treatment initiation while pulmonary and other symptom mentions persisted. Source-reported correlations with structured-data trends were .80 for treatment and .92 for glomerulonephritis.
evidence.unknown: This is one retrospective healthcare-system cohort of prevalent PR3/MPO-ANCA-positive cases, with no non-vasculitis comparator or independent clinical validation. Before-treatment notes were fewer and involved fewer patients. Topic scores are fractions of assigned words within pooled documentation windows, not patient risks or incidence; copy-and-paste, templates, note density and outside-system care can affect trends. Psychiatric symptoms and diagnostic delays were already known in vasculitis; this analysis does not establish their first discovery. No causal treatment effect or prospective diagnostic performance is shown.
evidence.ai_role: Unsupervised learned word-topic distributions expose documentation themes and temporal contrasts that would be missed by restricting analysis to structured codes.

source_review.scope: Original cohort definition, note preparation, learned topic generation, statistical trend analysis, full represented Results and Discussion limitations actually read.
